analysis.evidence: הַנְּפִלִים is the subject of הָיוּ בָאָרֶץ, “were on the earth.” The phrase בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם וְגַם אַחֲרֵי כֵן places them “in those days and also afterward.” The verse goes on to speak of הַגִּבֹּרִים, “the mighty men,” as אַנְשֵׁי הַשֵּׁם, “men of renown.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הַ־.
analysis.sense: Nephilim, a group associated with the mighty men of old

analysis.evidence: הָיוּ agrees with the plural subject הַנְּפִלִים. The phrase בָאָרֶץ gives their location, and בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם gives the time: “The Nephilim were on the earth in those days.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural
analysis.sense: to be present in a place

analysis.evidence: In הַנְּפִלִים הָיוּ בָאָרֶץ, בָאָרֶץ tells where the Nephilim were, and בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם tells when. The earth is the setting for their presence, with no particular territory in view.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article, followed by a common noun, singular absolute, of common gender.

analysis.evidence: The plural demonstrative הָהֵם modifies בַּיָּמִים. Together they mean ‘in those days’ and identify the period when the Nephilim were on earth. וְגַם אַחֲרֵי כֵן ‘and also afterward’ distinguishes that period from a later one.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with prefixed בְּ ‘in’ and the definite article הַ.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

analysis.evidence: גַּם adds אַחֲרֵי כֵן ‘afterward’ to בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם ‘in those days’. The Nephilim were on the earth in those days and also afterward.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ־ ‘and’ prefixed to the additive particle גַּם.

analysis.evidence: בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם means “in those days.” וְגַם אַחֲרֵי כֵן adds “and also after that,” with כֵן referring back to those days.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם (‘in those days’) supplies the time to which כֵן points back. וְגַם אַחֲרֵי כֵן (‘and also after that’) extends the statement about the Nephilim beyond those days.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם וְגַם אַחֲרֵי כֵן sets the time frame, “in those days and also afterward.” אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause that describes what happened during that time, hence “when the sons of God went in to the daughters of humankind.”
analysis.morphology: Invariant relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The sons of God are the subject of יָבֹאוּ, and אֶל־בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם identifies the women they went in to. The next clause, וְיָלְדוּ לָהֶם, says that the women bore them children, confirming the sexual sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural, with י־ and plural ending ־וּ.
analysis.sense: go in to a woman for sexual intercourse

analysis.evidence: In בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים, “the sons of God,” בְּנֵי is the construct form of “sons,” and הָאֱלֹהִים names the one to whom they belong. The parallel phrase בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם means “the daughters of humankind.” The plural verb יָבֹאוּ agrees with the sons.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: In יָבֹאוּ … אֶל בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם, אֶל introduces the women to whom the sons of God came. The following וְיָלְדוּ לָהֶם (“and they bore children to them”) indicates that בוא אֶל here refers to sexual relations.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם means “the daughters of humankind.” Its pairing with בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים, “the sons of God,” identifies the daughters by their membership in humanity.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The daughters of humankind are the subject of וְיָלְדוּ. They bore children to the sons of God, whom לָהֶם (‘to them’) refers to. The children are understood from the verb.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with prefixed conjunction וְ. The form continues יָבֹאוּ in a sequence describing repeated events.

analysis.evidence: הֵמָּה הַגִּבֹּרִים means “they were the mighty men.” The verse calls them אַנְשֵׁי הַשֵּׁם, “men of renown,” identifying them as the heroes of old.
analysis.morphology: Adjective used substantivally, masculine plural absolute, with the definite article הַ־.
analysis.sense: warrior, mighty man of war, champion

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying הַגִּבֹּרִים. The clause has no expressed verb, so הַגִּבֹּרִים אֲשֶׁר מֵעוֹלָם reads “the mighty men who were of old.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse looks back to בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם, “in those days.” In הַגִּבֹּרִים אֲשֶׁר מֵעוֹלָם, “the mighty men who were of old,” מֵעוֹלָם places these men in the distant past.
analysis.morphology: Preposition מִן, realized as מֵ־, prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: אַנְשֵׁי takes הַשֵּׁם as its complement. The phrase אַנְשֵׁי הַשֵּׁם, “men of renown,” describes the mighty men of old by their reputation.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct noun, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: man of …: one marked by a quality, calling or people
